articles.content:
BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM

Dolly Parton launched the Imagination Library in 1995 on a premise that hasn’t changed since: send a free book to every registered child under five, once a month, for the first years of their life. No application, no means test, no reading assessment required. It’s as simple as a book, addressed to the child by name, showing up in the mailbox.

Thirty-one years and 330 million books later, the program is still growing; Now it’s growing without her.

Parton died earlier this year. Less than a month later, the Imagination Library announced it’s doubling its London presence, going from five of the city’s 32 boroughs to 10. That makes 157,000 more children eligible for a book every month.

A program built to go beyond its founder

Jeff Conyers, president of the Dollywood Foundation, said Parton would have been “incredibly proud.” “Dolly always wanted the Imagination Library to be something that lived on for generations into the future,” he told the BBC. “She was constantly pushing us about how we get the Imagination Library to more and more children and more and more families.”

The London expansion is funded by the Postcode Lottery, a U.K. charity lottery. Clara Govier, the Postcode Lottery’s managing director for the U.K., said Parton “understood the extraordinary power of something very simple: a child, a grown-up, and a book.”

The Imagination Library doesn’t approach reading through apps or skill assessments. It just gets books into homes. The program’s research shows parents say their kids become more interested in reading once the monthly books start arriving, and some studies find those children develop stronger literacy skills than peers who didn’t enroll.

Falling reading scores on both sides of the Atlantic

Early childhood literacy is going the wrong way in both the U.S. and the U.K. The most recent National Assessment of Educational Progress data puts 33 percent of U.S. eighth graders at “below basic” reading levels, the highest in the test’s 30-year history. Forty percent of fourth graders scored the same, the worst result in two decades.

In the U.K., a survey of 1,000 teachers found that nearly a third of preschool-age children can’t properly interact with a physical book. They tap and swipe at the pages as though they were touchscreens. These kids aren’t uninterested in stories, they’re just distracted by the devices that get there first.

From one Tennessee county to 10 London boroughs

The Imagination Library started in Parton’s home county of Sevier County, Tennessee. It now runs across all 50 U.S. states and in Canada, Australia, Ireland, and the United Kingdom. The model travels because it comes down to one thing: find a local funder, cover the books, and the Dollywood Foundation handles the rest. No bespoke infrastructure, no rebuilding from scratch.

The London expansion works the same way: the Postcode Lottery covers the new boroughs while The Dollywood Foundation provides the infrastructure.

What Parton built was simple enough to cross borders and durable enough to keep going after she was gone. London now covers 10 of its 32 boroughs.

This expansion in London benefits 157,000 more children, addressing a critical issue of declining reading skills in both the U.S. and U.K. The program's broad reach, measurable positive impact on literacy, and sustainable model continuing beyond its founder's life make it genuinely inspiring and impactful.
articles.personality_title: Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library doubles its reach in London after her passing
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Dolly Parton started the Imagination Library in 1995 to send free books every month to children under five. The goal was simple: help young kids learn to love reading by giving them books at home, without any complicated sign-up process.

**What happened** – After Dolly Parton’s death earlier this year, the program announced it is now available in twice as many parts of London. It has grown from five to ten boroughs, meaning 157,000 more young children will get free books every month.

**Impact** – This expansion is important because reading skills are dropping in both the U.S. and the U.K. Studies show children who receive books through the program enjoy reading more and build better literacy skills than those who don’t. The program’s simple approach—delivering books directly to kids—works without needing apps or tests.

**What’s next step** – The Imagination Library will continue to grow in London and other countries. Local groups pay for the books, while the program manages sending them out. This way, the program can keep reaching more children without needing Dolly Parton herself to run it.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library keeps helping hundreds of thousands of children learn to read by doubling its reach in London and continuing to grow worldwide.
articles.personality_title_fr: La bibliothèque d’imagination de Dolly Parton double sa portée à Londres après son décès
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Dolly Parton a lancé la Bibliothèque d’imagination en 1995 pour envoyer chaque mois des livres gratuits aux enfants de moins de cinq ans. Le but était simple : aider les jeunes enfants à aimer la lecture en leur donnant des livres à la maison, sans démarches compliquées.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Après la mort de Dolly Parton plus tôt cette année, le programme a annoncé qu’il est désormais disponible dans deux fois plus de quartiers à Londres. Il est passé de cinq à dix arrondissements, ce qui signifie que 157 000 enfants supplémentaires recevront des livres gratuits chaque mois.

**Impact** – Cette expansion est importante car les compétences en lecture baissent aux États-Unis et au Royaume-Uni. Des études montrent que les enfants qui reçoivent des livres grâce au programme aiment plus la lecture et développent de meilleures compétences que ceux qui n’en bénéficient pas. L’approche simple du programme – livrer les livres directement aux enfants – fonctionne sans applications ni tests.

**Prochaine étape** – La Bibliothèque d’imagination continuera de se développer à Londres et dans d’autres pays. Des groupes locaux paient les livres, tandis que le programme s’occupe de les envoyer. Ainsi, le programme peut toucher de plus en plus d’enfants sans que Dolly Parton soit là pour le gérer.

**Résumé en une phrase** – La Bibliothèque d’imagination de Dolly Parton continue d’aider des centaines de milliers d’enfants à apprendre à lire en doublant sa portée à Londres et en grandissant dans le monde.
articles.personality_title_es: La Biblioteca de la Imaginación de Dolly Parton duplica su alcance en Londres tras su fallecimiento
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Dolly Parton comenzó la Biblioteca de la Imaginación en 1995 para enviar libros gratis cada mes a niños menores de cinco años. La idea era sencilla: ayudar a los niños pequeños a amar la lectura entregándoles libros en casa, sin trámites complicados.

**Qué pasó** – Después de la muerte de Dolly Parton a principios de este año, el programa anunció que ahora está disponible en el doble de áreas en Londres. Pasó de cinco a diez distritos, lo que significa que 157,000 niños más recibirán libros gratis cada mes.

**Impacto** – Esta expansión es importante porque las habilidades de lectura están bajando tanto en Estados Unidos como en Reino Unido. Los estudios muestran que los niños que reciben libros a través del programa disfrutan más la lectura y desarrollan mejores habilidades que los que no lo hacen. El programa funciona simplemente entregando los libros directamente a los niños, sin necesidad de aplicaciones o pruebas.

**Próximo paso** – La Biblioteca de la Imaginación seguirá creciendo en Londres y otros países. Grupos locales pagan los libros, mientras el programa se encarga de enviarlos. Así, el programa puede llegar a más niños sin que Dolly Parton tenga que estar presente.

**Resumen en una frase** – La Biblioteca de la Imaginación de Dolly Parton sigue ayudando a cientos de miles de niños a aprender a leer al duplicar su alcance en Londres y continuar creciendo en todo el mundo.
